rv.q: This lends an unnecessarily oppressive air to a play that’s actually all about liberation and making choices.
The story unfolds without any surprises.
This play may be a tad dated, but I found it involving throughout, even if the denouement is rather obvious and its two hour length just right.
London is lucky to have a third opportunity to see this fascinating and emotional play which has been staged beautifully.

A PLAY’S success can be judged by assessing the snack you brought in, once the actors take their final bow. If the forgotten packet of melted milk chocolate buttons is anything to go by, Coming Clean had me engrossed. It’s a touching script from 1982 by Kevin Elyot (My Night with Reg) but feels relevant and fresh almost 40 years later.
Coming Clean is nevertheless a triumph in delivering Elyot’s quick wit and emotional depth...

cn.t: Elyot's 1982 debut receives a warm but mixed revival, with critics praising its touching depiction of pre-AIDS gay relationships and mature writing, though some find it baggy and over-directed at times.
